newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended firmer, consolidating a recovery from recent declines. December ended $0.80 a tonne higher at $328.00, while second month March finished at $329.00, up $1.00. In New York raw sugar futures ended little changed after yesterday's selloff. October closed 3 points lower at 11.40 cents/lb, while the back months added 2 to 5 points. There was no fresh news to influence prices.

POLAND - The first Polish beet test (September 2) confirms that the country will have a better crop than last year. Root weight on September 2 reached 732 grams, 10 per cent more than last year and 41 per cent above 1994. However, sugar content was at 13.78 per cent somewhat lower than last year (14.34 per cent). But thanks to the high root weight, sugar per root reached 101 grams, up from 95 grams last year. As there is no information on plant density it is impossible to calculate the theoretical sugar yield per ha. The beet area is with 450,000 ha significantly up on last year's figure of 378,000 ha. Sugar production in 1996/97 (September/August) is estimated at roughly 2 million tonnes in raw value terms up from 1.7 million tonnes in 1995/96 and 1.5 million tonnes in 1994/95. This means that the country will have a considerable sugar surplus this season, possibly exceeding 200,000 tonnes in raw value terms.

UNITED KINGDOM - Sugar imports in June 1996 amounted to 111,221 tonnes, raw value, against 145,146 tonnes in June 1995. This brought cumulative imports in the first nine months of 1995/96 (October/June) up to 1,003,925 tonnes against 1,092,358 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1994/95 reached 1.47 million tonnes compared to 1.34 million tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of origin in the first three quarters of 1995/96 were Mauritius with 372,951 tonnes raws against 343,767 tonnes, Guyana with 134,296 tonnes compared to 128,400 tonnes, Fiji with 125,680 tonnes compared to 115,600 tonnes and Jamaica with 125,226 tonnes against 113,380 tonnes. Sugar exports in June 1996 amounted to 34,737 tonnes, down from 67,427 tonnes exported in June 1995. This brought cumulative exports in October/June 1995/96 up to 292,003 tonnes against 392,694 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1994/95 amounted to 560,076 tonnes, up from 537,317 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of destination in October/June 1995/96 were Israel with 88,718 tonnes whites compared to 102,537 tonnes, Norway with 35,069 tonnes compared to 28,150 tonnes and Italy with 25,011 tonnes against 23,345 tonnes. Sugar consumption in April 1996 reached 183,696 tonnes, slightly up on last year's 180,652 tonnes. This brought cumulative consumption in the first seven months of 1995/96 (October/April) up to 1.27 million tonnes, down from 1.34 million tonnes in the same period last year. Total consumption in 1994/95 reached 2.38 million tonnes against 2.43 million tonnes in 1993/94.

SOUTH KOREA - Sugar imports in May 1996 amounted to 85,808 tonnes, raw value, down from 107,178 tonnes in May 1995. This brought cumulative imports in the first five months of 1996 (January/May) up to 570,331 tonnes against 529,933 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995 amounted to 1.31 million tonnes compared to 1.27 million tonnes in 1994. Major countries of origin in January/May 1996 were Thailand with 364,758 tonnes raws against 175,737 tonnes and Australia with 179,698 tonnes against 264,616 tonnes. Sugar exports in May 1996 reached 17,284 tonnes against 18,934 tonnes in May 1995. This brought cumulative exports in January/May 1996 up to 143,403 tonnes compared to 124,955 tonnes in January/May 1995. Major countries of destination in January/May 1996 were Hong Kong with 46,426 tonnes whites against 47,480 tonnes, Indonesia with 40,302 tonnes compared to 25,122 tonnes and Saudi Arabia with 26,001 tonnes against nil.

The European Union awarded 129,500 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 44.837 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on Wednesday. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to September 18 reached 313 250 tonnes, which compares to 593 025 tonnes last year. Tunisia bought two cargoes of 14,000 tonnes each of white sugar for May and July delivery at a snap tender on Wednesday, traders said. The price was not disclosed.
